post.hook: China ships big models; Anthropic eyes Nasdaq
post.subhook: Plus chip export rules, DeepSeek caps and a child-safety report

post.caption:
Chinese labs shipped big models today, and Anthropic is reportedly headed for Nasdaq.

1. Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max, saying it filtered training data to remove offensive cyber and CBRN capabilities. Artificial Analysis scores it 43 on its Intelligence Index. (South China Morning Post)
2. Anthropic's IPO is reported to debut on Nasdaq on Nov. 19, with coverage flagging limits on retail-investor access. (The Conversation)
3. Meituan releases open weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model trained on Chinese hardware without Nvidia GPUs. (The Decoder)
4. DeepSeek reportedly imposes daily quotas and shorter inputs amid chip shortages. DeepSeek has not confirmed. (Pandaily)
5. Congress moves to tighten AI chip export rules, including a bill to block Chinese companies from overseas chip access. (The Verge)
6. A Childlight report finds reports of AI-related child sexual abuse material rose 8,400% in two years, including deepfakes from nudify apps. (The Guardian)
7. Megaspeed reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies. (The Decoder)
8. Claude Opus 5.5 is now the default on paid plans, and Anthropic's new guidance says to drop 'think hard' prompts and start at Medium effort. (The Decoder)
9. Tencent releases Hy4 flash, a 224B model with 12B active parameters at 2 yuan per million output tokens. Main results are on Tencent's own benchmark. (Pandaily)

Chips and export rules ran through half of today's news.

clusters.headline: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max flagship model with cybersecurity and CBRN data filtering
clusters.why_it_matters: Alibaba says it filtered Qwen4-Max training data to remove offensive cyber and CBRN capabilities, and Artificial Analysis scores it 43 on its Intelligence Index, so developers can weigh it against rival models.

clusters.headline: Anthropic IPO reported to debut on Nasdaq on Nov. 19
clusters.why_it_matters: A public listing of a leading AI lab could change its funding, governance and regulatory scrutiny, and coverage flags retail-investor access limits.

clusters.headline: Meituan releases open weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model trained on Chinese hardware
clusters.why_it_matters: Open weights for a very large agent model trained without Nvidia GPUs give practitioners a new large open option and evidence of non-Nvidia training.

clusters.headline: DeepSeek reportedly imposes daily quotas and curbs chat access amid chip shortages
clusters.why_it_matters: Users of DeepSeek's app and web chat may face daily caps and shorter inputs, though DeepSeek has not confirmed the limits.

clusters.headline: Congress moves to tighten AI chip export rules, including a bill to block Chinese companies from overseas chip access
clusters.why_it_matters: Bipartisan support for tighter export rules could restrict which companies can access AI accelerators abroad.

clusters.headline: Reports of AI-related child sexual abuse material rise 8,400% in two years
clusters.why_it_matters: A Childlight report finds sharply rising reports of AI-generated abuse material, including deepfakes from nudify apps, which may push regulators toward stronger controls.

clusters.headline: Megaspeed reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies
clusters.why_it_matters: Reported chip orders routed to China through an intermediary could draw enforcement and export-control scrutiny of AI hardware supply.

clusters.headline: Anthropic makes Claude Opus 5.5 default on paid plans and publishes new prompting guidance
clusters.why_it_matters: Paid users now default to Opus 5.5, and the guide advises dropping think hard prompts and starting at Medium effort.
